transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it. 

Um, I guess what finally pushed me to make this appointment is... well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I'm an auditor and I'm supposed to be on top of everything. But I've been noticing this pattern where I'll start my follow-up items after an audit, or maybe after one of the mentorship events I run. And I have every single intention of finishing them right then and there. But then... I don't know, days later I'll find out that the final email never actually went out, or a review note or a form just never got completely done. 

It's not that I don't care about the work, I really do, and I usually catch it eventually. It's just... little things seem to slip through the cracks sometimes before I realize it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Did these attention or follow-through problems start when you were a child?

Um... well, yes. I suppose so. I mean, I was a really good kid, I promise! But... um, looking back at elementary school, my report cards always said I was bright, which was nice. But they would also usually have these little notes saying I, you know, lost assignments, or rushed past small details... or maybe talked out of turn a bit and needed reminders to finish my work. 

It wasn't anything terrible, just... a little scattered, I guess? My mother actually still jokes about it today. She always says I was the kind of kid who could completely ace a test, but then forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack. 

So... I guess the pattern has been there for a while. Is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you often feel physically restless or fidgety?

Um... well, I try very hard to sit still, especially at work, because I really don't want to distract anyone. But... yes, I suppose I do have a bit of nervous energy. 

When I'm sitting in long audit meetings, I'm usually tapping my foot under the table, or maybe just clicking my pen a little bit. I also end up shifting in my chair quite a lot. It's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but one of my colleagues even joked recently that she can hear my leg going under the desk when we're in the conference room. 

I really don't mean to do it, and I try to keep it hidden, it just sort of happens without me realizing. Is that what you mean by restless? I hope I'm answering that right.
Do these attention or follow-through problems interfere with your work, home life, or relationships?

Oh, um... well, I really try my best not to let it affect anyone else. I always want to be reliable, I really do. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has been causing some issues lately. It's actually really hard to admit this, but at work, some of those unfinished follow-ups I mentioned earlier... well, they actually affected a client review recently. I fixed it as fast as I could, I promise! But it was enough that... well, I've been so worried lately that people are starting to question whether I can actually handle the promotion I've been working toward. 

And at home... my husband is incredibly patient, he really is a wonderful man. But he's actually had to take over paying the bills and managing some of the household commitments I said I would handle. I always have every intention of doing them, but... he just can't really count on me to get them completed reliably right now, so he just took it all on himself. I feel terrible about it, honestly. I hate feeling like I'm letting him or my team down. 

Does that answer your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need, and I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is...
Before age 12, were you already having these kinds of attention or follow-through problems?

Um... yes, I think we touched on this just a little bit earlier, but... yes, definitely before I was 12. 

Like I mentioned, back in elementary school, I was a good student overall, I promise! My teachers always wrote that I was a bright girl on my report cards. But... they did always seem to include those little notes about me losing my assignments, or, you know, rushing through things and missing the small details. And they did have to remind me to finish my work quite a bit, or ask me to stop talking out of turn. 

It wasn't that I was trying to be difficult or anything! I just... I think my brain was just moving a little too fast. Like my mom still jokes about—how I would get a perfect score on a written test, but completely forget to hand in the big diorama project that was literally sitting right there in my backpack. 

So, yes, it was definitely happening back then. I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself a little bit... I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking!
Do you often interrupt other people before they finish speaking?

Um... well... I really try to be a good listener. I know how important it is to let people finish their thoughts, and I always want to be respectful of my colleagues. 

But... I guess, sometimes... yes, I do catch myself jumping in. It happens a lot with the junior auditors on my team. It's never because I don't care about what they're saying! It's just... when they're explaining something, an answer or an idea will pop into my head, and it just feels so urgent in that moment. It's almost like if I don't say it right then, I'll lose it completely. So I just sort of... blurt it out before I can even stop myself. 

I always apologize right after, and I tell them to please keep going! I hate doing it, because I know it probably seems rude, and I really don't want to be that kind of coworker. I just get so eager to help or solve the problem. 

Is that... does that count as what you're asking about? I really am working on being better about it, I promise.
As a child, were you often unable to stay seated when you were expected to?

Oh, um... you know, I really don't think so. I mean, I always tried very hard to be a good student and follow the rules, especially when the teacher was talking. 

I'm sure I probably wiggled around in my chair a bit, like any kid does, but I don't remember ever actually getting up and walking around when I wasn't supposed to. I would have been so embarrassed if I got in trouble for something like that! I always wanted my teachers to like me, so I really made an effort to stay in my seat during class. 

At least... that's how I remember it. I hope that's helpful? I just really don't think that was one of the things I struggled with back then.
Do these attention problems cause clear difficulty in your daily functioning, such as at work or at home?

Um... well... I guess I'd have to say yes. I mean, I really, really try to keep everything together, I promise I do! I don't want to sound like I'm completely falling apart or anything. 

But... at work... it has been getting a little hard. I've been making some mistakes, mostly just little things, but... well, some of my follow-ups haven't gotten finished when they were supposed to. And it actually affected a client review recently, which was just awful. I felt terrible about it. I've been up for a promotion, and I just worry so much that people are starting to question if I can handle it. I really am capable, I just... things slip through the cracks sometimes.

And at home... well, my husband is wonderful, he really is. But he's kind of had to take over paying the bills and handling a lot of the commitments I said I would do. I think he just... he feels like he can't count on me to actually finish them reliably right now. It's embarrassing to admit that, honestly. I want to be a good partner, I really do! 

Does that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, I'm just trying to be honest with you.
Do these attention and follow-through problems also happen outside of work, like in other parts of your life?

Um... outside of work and what I just mentioned about the house? I... I really don't think so. 

I try so hard to be a good friend and, you know, be dependable for the people in my life. I would just die of embarrassment if I was dropping the ball with my friendships or if I let someone down when they needed me. So I really put a lot of extra energy into making sure I show up and follow through for them. 

I haven't really noticed any big problems in those other areas, thankfully. At least, nobody has said anything to me about it, and I always try my absolute best to be as helpful and organized as I can be when it involves other people. 

Is that... does that answer your question? I hope it's a good sign that I'm managing okay in those parts of my life.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a lifelong pattern of inattention and impulsivity beginning in childhood, with current symptoms causing clear occupational and home impairment. She also reports mild hyperactive/restless features (fidgeting, shifting, tapping), but not the full picture of predominantly inattentive symptoms alone. This is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation (ICD-10 F90.0). R41.840 was considered but is less appropriate because the presentation is a developmental disorder with childhood onset and functional impairment, not merely an attention/concentration symptom.
